title: Playing with drummer Monk Hazel
summary: Bergen distinguishes the various Monks and praises Monk Hazel's drumming and reliability, including two drinking incidents.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Speaking of Monks, how many Monks were there around?

The only Monks I knew was Monk Hazel. I didn't meet him until later in life. And Monk Myers played saxophone I didn't know. And Norman Myers, some guys called him Monk Myers when he was in Jesuits. I don't know. Was Monk Hazel a ball player? Monk Barone was a ball player but he played saxophone a little bit in the old days. But Monk Hazel, he went to Jefferson School, I don't remember him there. Maybe he was a little older than me though.
Did he play any good? Who? Monk Hazel.
Man, you hear them tapes I got? Yeah. That's what made the tapes. Monk inspired you to play. You'd have to hold me on the bandstand sometimes. When you play with Monk you're jumping.
Monk makes you jump when you play.

He's everything they said about him. And I mean it proves it. I had one tape where I think he enjoyed playing with me because when we finished playing he said, wowee! And I know Monk, he told me at one time we had the best spot in jazz band in town. Coming from him I appreciate it. Because he was sitting in, not sitting in, but playing off nights in the quarter at that time. Yeah, Monk was a kick. But he sure could beat those drums.
Did he drink when he was with you?

I must say that his mother had just died and twice he drank a little bit. Both times he finished the jobs with me. And he might have had a little bit too near the end, but he finished the job, he got home, and I couldn't complain. And there's a funny thing, it was a year apart and it was the same job at the same place where it happened. In other words I booked the job one year and the next year I booked it and it was booked in the same place. And two times it happened. In fact on some of the jobs I had some big shots helping me out, you know, to play with my band. And he knows them real good. And he was saying, look at them, drinking. How are they going to play their horn?
How are they going to play their horn?

Yeah. He was almost a, what do you call it, who was that old lady? One of the Carrie Nation's boys there for a while. Yeah. When he was playing with me. Yeah, I had no trouble with Monk. Yeah. Showed up on every job and gee whiz anybody can drink twice in a year. Sure.
